summary: A fanout wave whose pending-ledger commit refuses for any reason still reports the verdict for the tags it already landed

per.section: The tick verdict — one facts artifact

acceptance: A ledger-commit refusal outside a parse failure returns a failed tick carrying the wave's verdict; the parse failure's exit 69 is unchanged.
tests: a ledger commit refusing outside a parse failure still carries the wave's shipped tags in its verdict
a ledger-commit refusal outside a parse failure is a failed tick, not a throw out of Dispatcher.tick
notes: commitPaths now runs `git commit --only`, which refuses on named paths with no change and on a partial commit under a paused merge or cherry-pick — both reachable from ordinary operator state, both landing on the catch that folds the verdict for PendingParseFailure alone and re-throws bare otherwise, losing tags already on trunk. Widen the carry rather than classify the cause: a disk error and an index.lock always took that arm too.

per.section: Narration is the ladder's bottom rung

acceptance: A renumbered docs section cannot leave a `§ N` on its own page standing, and a page with no numbered headings is silent rather than red.
tests: a `§ N` on a docs page resolves against that page's own numbered headings
a docs page with no numbered headings leaves its `§ N` as prose
notes: Ten docs pages carry numbered headings and `§ N` refs; CLI.md, INTENT.md and LAYERS.md carry none and take the prose arm. Refs aiming at another page's numbering (MIGRATING-0.11.md, CASCADE-DRY-RUN.md) are judged against their own page, the reading the rule states. The prior attempt reverted on the section-cite pin, not on its own work: its new comment illustrated the shape as a literal page-and-section pair, which that arm now reds — spell the placeholder `<page>.md`.
